content: 1. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the medications you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products. This is important because mifepristone can slow the elimination of other drugs from your body, potentially altering their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications can affect how mifepristone is removed from your body, which may impact its efficacy. 2. Mifepristone may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss alternative non-hormonal birth control methods with your doctor or pharmacist while using this medication. 3. Beta-blocker medications, such as metoprolol, propranolol, or glaucoma eye drops like timolol, may mask the symptoms of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), such as a rapid or pounding heartbeat. Many drugs can affect blood sugar levels, making it more challenging to manage. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist to understand how it may influence your blood sugar levels. 4. Regularly monitor your blood sugar levels as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high or low blood sugar. 5. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. For non-emergency cases, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 6. While taking this medication, your doctor may recommend laboratory or medical tests, such as potassium levels, thyroid function, and blood pressure, to monitor your health. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. 7. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 8. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 9. Mifepristone may cause dizziness. Avoid consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) as they can exacerbate this effect. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. 10. This medication may cause a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart rhythm. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using diuretics (water pills) or experiencing severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. 11. Mifepristone must not be used during pregnancy as it can cause pregnancy loss. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. 12. This medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding while using this medication. 13. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 14. This document provides a summary of information about mifepristone and does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
